key_idea: Enumerate every maximal empty rectangle exactly once with the histogram technique: for each bottom row, each distinct (height, left, right) span from the monotonic stack is maximal up/left/right, and is maximal downward iff the row below has an obstacle inside its column span.
sketch: For each row keep column heights of consecutive empty cells. With a monotonic stack compute for each column the nearest strictly lower column on the left and right; a column is canonical if there is no equal-height column between it and its left boundary, which deduplicates rectangles. A canonical column with h>0 gives rectangle of height h and width R-L-1 that cannot grow up, left or right; it cannot grow down iff it is the last row or a prefix-sum over the next row shows an obstacle in (L,R). Count it if (h>=s and w>=t) or (h>=t and w>=s). Complexity O(rc), 9e6 cells. Pitfalls: the size requirement is orientation-free, double counting of equal heights, and the bottom-maximality check. Stress-tested against an exhaustive brute force.
